fr.elements: Main Residence; Detached Structure; Detached Structure; Vehicle Parking Area; Access Drive; Detached Garage; Open Lawn Area; Dense Vegetation; Walkway
fr.considerations: Multiple Structures; Dense Vegetation; Limited Rear Access; Single Access Point
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance to help responders confirm the correct property from the road.
• Mark the access drive entry clearly so responders can identify it quickly on approach.
• Keep the access drive clear of parked vehicles so emergency equipment can reach all structures without obstruction.
• Trim dense vegetation along the access drive to maintain clear sightlines and prevent it from narrowing the travel path.
• Cut back dense vegetation near the detached structures so responders can move around and between buildings without obstruction.
• Post a simple site map at the driveway entrance showing the locations of all structures and the walkway connections between them.
• Keep walkways between structures clear so responders can move on foot between buildings quickly.
• Identify and mark any rear access points to the property so responders are aware of all available approach routes.
• If a rear gate exists, keep it unlocked or secured with a combination known to local emergency services.
• Stage a visible exterior address or unit identifier on each detached structure so responders can distinguish between buildings during an incident.

wildfire.conditions: Tree Cluster; Structure Surrounded by Vegetation; Vegetation Near Structure; Large Trees; Scattered Trees; Open Clearing; Vegetation Along Driveway; Limited Rear Access; Scattered Shrubs; Multiple Access Routes
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim branches from large trees that overhang or touch the roof and walls of the structure.
• Thin the tree cluster nearest to the structure to create open spacing between individual trees.
• Remove shrubs and low-growing plants growing directly against the foundation and walls of the structure.
• Separate scattered shrubs from the base of large trees so fire cannot climb from ground-level plants into the tree canopy.
• Clear dead leaves, branches, and plant debris from the roof and gutters regularly.
• Trim overhanging branches along the driveway to keep the full width and height clear for vehicle access.
• Remove or cut back shrubs and low branches along the driveway edges that narrow the travel path.
• Clear vegetation along the rear of the structure to open a path for movement and access around the building.
• Thin scattered trees on the approach to the structure to keep sightlines and movement paths open.
• Keep the open clearing free of encroaching shrubs or woody plants that are growing in from the edges.
• Remove dead wood, fallen branches, and dry plant material from beneath large trees near the structure.
• Mark or keep both access routes clearly visible and free of vegetation that could block entry or exit.
